regions.notes: Use sparingly near the hand/mask area on the right side of either panel if a third label is needed.

caption_guidance.pattern: The joke works by showing a fake or expected identity first, then revealing the surprising true identity underneath.

bad_examples.masked_identity: This is a very long sentence that will not fit well in the mask area

bad_examples.revealed_identity: Same thing as above, just repeated with no contrast or reveal

regions.role: setup text for the sleeping/indifferent state
regions.notes: Place over the upper-right image area, avoiding the face and the existing small 'i sleep' text if possible.

regions.role: punchline text for the awakened/intense state
regions.notes: Place over the lower-right image area, avoiding the face and the existing small 'real shit' text if possible.

caption_guidance.pattern: The joke contrasts a calm, uninterested reaction with an intense, awakened reaction when something unexpectedly becomes important or exciting.

regions.notes: Place in the open left side above and around the left Spider-Man, avoiding the face and body.
Use the upper middle area; keep text clear of the central Spider-Man's head and pointing arms.
Best placed in the upper-right open space; avoid the right Spider-Man and the crate.

caption_guidance.pattern: Three nearly identical characters point at each other to show escalating blame, disagreement, or self-contradiction across three labels.

bad_examples.left_spider_man: A very long sentence that wraps into five lines and covers the character

bad_examples.right_spider_man: Tiny caption placed over the crate and lower body

regions.role: setup or reaction text describing Squidward's viewpoint
regions.notes: Use the dark upper-left area; keep text away from Squidward's head silhouette.

regions.role: punchline or contrasting text about what Squidward sees
regions.notes: Place in the open window area above/around the characters, avoiding faces and the horizontal blinds.

caption_guidance.pattern: Use the left side for Squidward's reaction or setup, and the right side for the thing he is judging, admiring, or being annoyed by.

good_examples.top_reaction_caption: When you hear the party start

good_examples.right_window_caption: and it's your neighbors being loud again

bad_examples.top_reaction_caption: A long paragraph that covers Squidward's face and body

bad_examples.right_window_caption: Text placed directly over SpongeBob and Patrick's faces

regions.role: setup or situation text placed above the shocked face
regions.notes: Large blank white area is ideal for classic top caption text; keep centered and high contrast.

caption_guidance.pattern: Use a short setup that describes an expectation, then let the image deliver the surprised reaction.

good_examples.top_reaction_caption: Me opening the fridge for the 5th time expecting new food

bad_examples.top_reaction_caption: Tiny text placed over Pikachu's face or body

regions.notes: Place text inside the white speech bubble on the top panel; keep away from the black outline and notch.
Place text inside the white speech bubble on the middle panel; avoid the outline and the left notch.

caption_guidance.pattern: The first two panels present a claim and a response, while the third panel shows the driver’s shocked realization or punchline reaction.

bad_examples.top_speech_bubble: A long paragraph that fills the whole bubble and becomes unreadable.

bad_examples.middle_speech_bubble: Text placed outside the bubble over the character’s face or car interior.

regions.role: main punchline text on the revealed scroll
regions.notes: Place text inside the blank parchment area; keep margins away from the decorative top and bottom flourishes.

regions.role: setup or discovery line in the opening panel
regions.notes: Fits the speech bubble area in the top-left panel; avoid the bubble tail and edges.

caption_guidance.pattern: Use the top-left bubble as the setup and the scroll as the reveal, with the joke landing on whatever absurd or disappointing 'truth' is written on the scroll.

good_examples.scroll_text:
IT WAS JUST
A REALLY LONG
ERROR MESSAGE

bad_examples.scroll_text: A single word that doesn't use the scroll reveal

regions.role: setup / outsider who knows the truth
regions.notes: Place above or around the standing figure on the left; avoid covering the face and cup.

regions.role: group being ignored / the people who don't know
regions.notes: Best for a short label describing the unaware pair in the lower-left corner; keep clear of heads and arms.

regions.role: main subject / the oblivious couple on the right
regions.notes: Use for the central joke text about what the couple does not realize; avoid the heads and shoulders.

caption_guidance.pattern: The joke contrasts one person who knows something important with the others who are oblivious to it.

good_examples.top_left_observer: Me knowing the group chat is about to explode

good_examples.right_couple:
Everyone else
still acting normal
while the drama
is already happening

bad_examples.top_left_observer: A long paragraph explaining the entire backstory

bad_examples.bottom_left_pair: Tiny text placed over the faces and arms

regions.role: setup text describing the two items being compared
regions.notes: Place over the dark band between the two top images; keep text short and high-contrast.

regions.role: punchline reveal that the two things are identical
regions.notes: Use the lower center area above the bottom edge; avoid covering the face.

caption_guidance.pattern: Present two supposedly different things in the top panel, then reveal in the bottom panel that they are actually the same.

good_examples.top_comparison_caption: My boss's 'urgent' request vs. my actual workload

bad_examples.top_comparison_caption: A long paragraph explaining the entire office politics situation in detail

bad_examples.bottom_reveal_caption: This is a completely unrelated joke with no comparison or reveal

regions.notes: Place short reaction text inside the existing speech bubble area; keep it concise and centered.
Use for a short caption spanning the lower margin; avoid covering the dog or flames too much.

caption_guidance.pattern: The joke is a calm, deadpan statement or caption placed over a chaotic disaster scene, creating irony by pretending everything is normal.

good_examples.bottom_caption: Me at work after deleting the wrong file

bad_examples.speech_bubble_text: A long multi-line paragraph about my entire day

bad_examples.bottom_caption: Tiny text crammed into the flames with no contrast

regions.role: header title announcing the meme setup
regions.notes: Place over the existing top banner area; keep short and bold.

regions.role: left-side offer label for what the speaker gets
regions.notes: Position in the upper-left open space above the subject's head.

regions.role: right-side offer label for what the other party gets
regions.notes: Position in the upper-right open space above the subject's head.

caption_guidance.pattern: Use the top title to frame a trade, then contrast a desirable 'i receive' item with an absurd, worse, or overly specific 'you receive' item.

bad_examples.i_receive: something long and sentence-like that wraps too much
bad_examples.you_receive: another long sentence that crowds the face

bad_examples.i_receive: text placed over the subject's face
bad_examples.you_receive: text placed over the subject's hands

regions.role: setup or plain reaction text for the unimpressed top panel
regions.notes: Keep text within the left half; avoid Pooh's face and the chair edge.

regions.role: punchline or upgraded reaction text for the smug bottom panel
regions.notes: Keep text within the left half; avoid the tuxedoed body and face.

caption_guidance.pattern: Use the top panel for a neutral, unimpressed, or low-status reaction, then use the bottom panel for the same character looking more confident, refined, or smug after an upgrade or realization.

bad_examples.top_reaction: A very long sentence that fills the whole panel and covers Pooh's face

bad_examples.bottom_reaction: Text placed on the right side over the blank white area, making the joke feel disconnected

regions.notes: Place text in the blank white panel above/around the left red button; keep clear of the button itself.
Place text in the blank white panel above/around the right red button; keep clear of the button itself.

regions.role: reaction or dilemma text on the sweating man
regions.notes: Use for the character's internal conflict, panic, or punchline; avoid covering the face too heavily if possible.

caption_guidance.pattern: The joke comes from presenting two undesirable or tempting options on the buttons, then showing the character sweating over which one to choose.

good_examples.reaction_caption: Why is this suddenly the hardest decision of my life?
I can only pick one and that feels illegal

bad_examples.left_button_label: A very long sentence that won't fit
bad_examples.right_button_label: Another overly long sentence that won't fit

bad_examples.reaction_caption: Text that tries to label every part of the image and covers the face and buttons

regions.role: label for the desirable or correct choice on the left side
regions.notes: Place over the sky/upper-left area; avoid the castle silhouette.

regions.role: label for the tempting, bad, or chaotic choice on the right side
regions.notes: Place over the dark sky/upper-right area; avoid the castle and lightning.

regions.role: main punchline or narrator text describing the choice being made
regions.notes: Use the open lower-center path area above the character; keep text clear of the signpost and boy.

caption_guidance.pattern: Use the two upper labels to contrast a good/safe option versus a bad/chaotic option, then add a bottom caption that frames the decision or reveals the punchline.

bad_examples.decision_caption: Me choosing the option that will definitely ruin my week

regions.role: setup text on the UNO card to present the choice or rule
regions.notes: Place text inside the blank white center of the left card; keep it short and bold.

regions.role: reaction text describing the person on the right or the consequence of the draw
regions.notes: Use the open wall area above/near the player; avoid covering the face and cards.

regions.role: punchline or commentary about the game state
regions.notes: Best for a short punchline placed over the empty table area.

caption_guidance.pattern: Use the left card as the setup and the right-side player as the reaction, with the joke landing on the absurdity of being forced to draw 25 cards.

bad_examples.top_left_card_text: a very long paragraph that won't fit
bad_examples.right_player_reaction: overlapping the man's face and cards

bad_examples.bottom_table_comment: covering the UNO logo or card edges

regions.notes: Use the open sky/grass area above the skeleton; keep text away from the head.
Place over the bench/empty lower area; avoid the hands and pelvis if possible.

caption_guidance.pattern: A setup describes waiting, delay, or anticipation, and the punchline reveals the wait has become absurdly long or pointless.

good_examples.top_caption: Me waiting for the update:

good_examples.bottom_caption: It's been 3 business eternities.

bad_examples.top_caption: Tiny text placed over the skull and face.

bad_examples.bottom_caption: A long paragraph that covers the entire skeleton.

caption_guidance.pattern: This is mainly a reaction image, so the joke comes from pairing the monkeys' blank, confused stares with a caption about not understanding or searching for something.

regions.notes: Place over the top panel; keep text away from the ear and mouth edges, centered in the open skin area.
Place over the bottom panel; use the smooth skin area as a clean backdrop for the reaction text.

caption_guidance.pattern: The top text is a whispered setup, and the bottom text is the physical reaction or consequence it causes.

good_examples.goosebumps_text: AND NOW MY SKIN IS PANICKING

bad_examples.goosebumps_text: A detailed paragraph about taxes and municipal bonds

regions.role: left-side accusation or emotional reaction text
regions.notes: Place over the left half, keeping clear of faces as much as possible; best for the dramatic complaint or accusation.

regions.role: right-side deadpan response or absurd counterpoint text
regions.notes: Place over the right half above the cat and table area; keep text away from the cat's face and the hand.

caption_guidance.pattern: Use the left side for an intense accusation or overreaction and the right side for a calm, clueless, or absurdly literal response.

good_examples.woman_yelling:
ME EXPLAINING
WHY THIS IS WRONG

bad_examples.cat_response: long paragraph that won't fit in the box

templates.name: Y'all Got Any More Of That
aliases: Y'all Got Any More Of That

regions.notes: Place over the open sky/background area; keep clear of the face and hat.
Use the lower empty band; avoid covering the hand and jacket.

caption_guidance.pattern: A character urgently asks for more of something, usually after running out, and the joke is the exaggerated desperation or scarcity.

good_examples.top_caption: WHEN THE GROUP CHAT DROPS THE LAST MEME

good_examples.bottom_caption: Y'ALL GOT ANY MORE OF THAT?

bad_examples.top_caption: A DETAILED PARAGRAPH ABOUT OFFICE POLICY

bad_examples.bottom_caption: THIS IS A SERIOUS HISTORICAL ANALYSIS

regions.notes: Place the first 'Yo dawg...' clause here; keep it short and centered above the face.
Use for the second clause that mirrors or escalates the setup; avoid covering the chain and shoulders too much.

caption_guidance.pattern: The joke is a recursive 'Yo dawg' setup where the first line introduces a thing and the second line absurdly duplicates or nests it.

good_examples.top_hook: YO DAWG, I HEARD YOU LIKE MEMES

good_examples.bottom_punchline: SO I PUT A MEME INSIDE YOUR MEME

bad_examples.top_hook: A RANDOM LONG PARAGRAPH ABOUT TECHNICAL SUPPORT

bad_examples.bottom_punchline: THIS IS A SERIOUS QUOTE WITH NO RECURSIVE TWIST
